To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
caveolin 3, a member of the caveolin gene family is expressed by endothelium, pericytes and astrocytes in brain microvessles.

in the human cortex, caveolin 1 was detected in the endothelium and the pericytes of the microvessles, and that caveolin 3, a subtype of caveolin 2, is expressed by the astrocytes surrounding the microvessells.
caveolin 3 is expressed in the cells forming the cerebral microvessels in the human cerebral cortex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the cellular localization of caveolin 3 in human brain cortex microvessles by immunofluorecence confocal microscopy, immunogold electronmicroscopy and Western blotting.
the identification of the site(s) where caveolin 1, the main caveolar protein, is expressed in the brain microvessel wall.
the identification of the site of cellular expression of the caveolin 1 protein in the human brain microvessel wall.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
caveolin 3 is a marker of astrocytes in the brain, caveolin 1 of endothelial cells, and caveolin 2 of pericytes, but that all caveolin subtypes are also found in the brain microvessel wall.

caveolin 2 is expressed in the endothelium of the cerebral microvasculature, while caveolin 3 is present in astroglial cells, and that both caveolin 2 and caveolin 3 are involved in the formation of caveolae in the cerebral endothelium and astroglia.
the endothelium, pericyte layer, and astrocytes of brain microvessles express caveolin 1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the expression of caveolin in brain microvessles is not limited to endothelial cells, but is also present in the pericytes and astrocytes of the vascular wall, suggesting a role of caveolin in the blood brain barrier.

caveolin 2 is expressed in endothelial cells and in pericytes, while caveolin 1 expression occurs in all the microvessel wall cells, i.e. endothelial cells, vascular astrocytes and pericytes, suggesting a role for caveolin 1 as a marker of the brain microvascular wall.

caveolae are present in the brain microvessel wall, where they may be involved in endothelial cell transport and metabolism, in the transcytosis of molecules and in endothelium cell signal transduction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
caveolin 2 is a key player in the development of the blood brain barrier.
caveolin 2 is expressed in the brain and in the brain microvessel endothelium.
caveolin 3 is expressed by astrocytes in the brain, but caveolin 1 expression is restricted to cells of the microvessel wall.
